title: Connection to Azure AD or Entra ID clients
author: domy86
body_snippet: Related to the issue https://github.com/mRemoteNG/mRemoteNG/issues/2329, how to connect using Azure AD web account? Remote clients have the most secured setup like NLA, NTLM v2 and so on. If I try to connect, I get this error: mRemote...

comments.author: robertpopa22
comments.snippet:
Labeled as feature request. Needs design before implementation — RDP over Entra ID requires hooking into the Windows Hello / WAM token flow, which is not something the existing RDP ActiveX control exposes directly. Tracking.

If anyone reading this has a working registry / GPO recipe that makes `mstsc.exe` consume an Entra ID credential at launch, please drop it in the thread — that would let us wire a lightweight bridge without reimplementing the auth stack.

comments.author: robertpopa22
comments.snippet:
Labeled as `enhancement` and kept on the roadmap. Realistic design before we can wire this in.

**Blocker right now:** the RDP ActiveX control mRemoteNG embeds (`MSTSCLib`) does not accept an Entra ID / Windows Hello token directly. Stock `mstsc.exe` picks up Entra creds via Windows Credential Manager + Conditional Access; the ActiveX in-process embedding path has no analogous hook in .NET.

comments.author: robertpopa22
comments.snippet:
@domy86 — Entra ID support shipped in commit `2e40adc6b` on `main` (full RDP pipeline: XML/CSV/SQL roundtrip + `enablerdsaadauth:i:1` emitted in .rdp export + live `IMsRdpExtendedSettings.Property["EnableRdsAadAuth"]` on the MSTSC ActiveX control). Same PR also adds WebAuthn/FIDO2 redirection since both use the same plumbing.

Available in the latest nightly: https://github.com/robertpopa22/mRemoteNG/releases/tag/nightly (build timestamp >= 2026-04-23).
